answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A reputation-weighted escrow contract releases payment only after independent counterparties attest to completed work; proven collusion or fraud burns the stake and reduces future access. Spinning up a hundred aliases then means funding a hundred deposits, while coordinating them risks losing the funds. Even an atlas of agents in an oasis-like market cannot make one island of fake accounts cheap: the attacker must pay real capital and bear real, enforceable loss.
